To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the c-fes protooncogene is involved in the differentiation process of HL60 cells induced by PMA, as shown by antisense oligodeoxynutcleotides (ODNs) inhibition of c-festhe expression.
c-fes protooncogene expression is required for macrophage differentiation.
antisense oligodeoxynuclotide-mediated inactivation of c-fes protein blocks the phorbol ester-induced differentiation of HL60 promyelocytie and of FDC-P1/ MAC-11 myeloid precursor cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel function for c-fes protooncogene in the differentiation program of myeloid cells.
a better understanding of c-fes role in the differentiation of myeloid cells and in the regulation of the adhesion properties of macrophages.
a novel function for c-fes in the differentiation process of myeloid cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-fes is required for the expression of the macrophage phenotype.
in HL60 cells c-fes is a necessary component of the differentiation pathway, but not a sufficient one, and that the differentiation program in HL60 cells is a multicomponent system.
c-fes protein is required in HL60 and FCD-P1/MAC11 cells for macrophage differentiation to occur.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the presence of phorbol ester, c-fes is required for myeloid differentiation.
c-fes is required for the differentiation process, but not for the growth control of myeloid cells.
in HL60 cells c-fes is a positive regulator of macrophage maturation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
c-Fes is a crucial component of the differentiation machinery of myeloid cells.
c-fes expression is required for phorbol ester-induced macrophage maturation in HL60 and FCD-P1/MAC11 cells.
c-fes is a critical regulator of macrophage maturation.
